job.title: Lead Planner
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an ASX-listed Australian gold development company focused on advancing a significant brownfields project in Western Australia.

Following a successful capital raise and project acquisition, the company has refocused its strategy on progressing the asset toward development and establishing itself as a mid-tier Australian gold producer.

With drilling, technical studies and optimisation work underway, the project is currently progressing through pre-feasibility activities, with a pathway toward potential first production in 2028, subject to required studies, approvals and development decisions.
  
The Opportunity
 
This will be a Perth based role with travel to site as required, the Lead Planner will take ownership of the development, integration and control of the project schedule as the asset progresses from studies through development and execution.

Reporting to the Project Controls Manager, the role will be responsible for establishing and maintaining the integrated project schedule across engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning and handover. A key priority will be developing a robust baseline schedule that provides clear visibility of project logic, critical-path activities, milestones, interfaces and delivery risks.

The role will work closely with project management, engineering, commercial, site and contractor teams to ensure planning inputs are accurate, integrated and aligned with the project’s delivery strategy.

About You

You will be an experienced Lead Planner or accomplished Senior Planner with strong hands-on scheduling capability and the confidence to take ownership of planning.

You will ideally bring:
  • At least five years’ planning and scheduling experience within mining, resources, infrastructure or major capital projects
  • Experience as a Lead Planner, or as a Senior Planner with responsibility for independently developing and controlling complex project schedules
  • Demonstrated experience developing baseline schedules from project scope, WBS and delivery strategy
  • Advanced Primavera P6 capability
  • Strong understanding of schedule logic, critical-path analysis, float, progress measurement and forecasting
  • Experience integrating engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning schedules
  • Strong cost and schedule integration capability
  • Experience reviewing and integrating contractor schedules
  • Greenfields or brownfields mining project experience, ideally across study and execution phases
  • A relevant qualification in engineering, project management, construction management or a related discipline 
Why This Role

This is an excellent  opportunity to join a fast-moving ASX-listed gold development company, giving employees the chance to be part of a company scaling up toward mid-tier producer status. On offer it an excellent salary package commensurate to experience.

Please apply via the “Apply for this job” button or online at www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference number 1034135.  For initial enquiries or assistance with your application, please contact Aaron Hooper at ahooper@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Site Supervisor
job.description:
The Company

Earthscape Technologies is an innovative Australian business delivering practical construction, engineering and manufacturing solutions across a range of industries. Its capabilities include mobile roll forming, long-span structural cladding and specialist systems for feedlots and agricultural projects, with a focus on creating simpler, safer and more cost-effective outcomes.

The Opportunity

Earthscape Technologies is seeking an experienced Site Supervisor to lead the day-to-day delivery of construction activities across regional and remote project sites. Working on a 3 weeks on / 1 week off roster, you will coordinate specialist trades, maintain site productivity and ensure projects are completed safely, efficiently, to specification and within agreed timeframes and budgets.

This is a practical, hands-on position for someone who can take ownership of site performance, solve problems quickly and build productive relationships with subcontractors, customers and project stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
  • Plan and oversee daily construction activities in line with drawings, specifications, schedules and quality standards
  • Coordinate concrete, structural steel, electrical and earthworks contractors
  • Monitor progress, resolve site constraints and implement practical solutions to keep projects moving
  • Manage labour, equipment, materials and trade sequencing to minimise downtime and unnecessary costs
  • Lead site safety, including inductions, pre-starts, SWMS, risk assessments, permits and compliance requirements
  • Monitor workmanship, subcontractor performance, productivity and site-level costs
  • Identify scope changes, variations and emerging commercial issues
  • Maintain accurate site records, progress reports, inspection documentation and project communications
  • Build positive relationships with rural and agricultural customers while minimising disruption to their operations
About You

This role will suit a capable construction supervisor with strong trade coordination, safety leadership and commercial awareness. You will be comfortable working independently in regional and remote environments and taking a practical approach to project delivery.

We would like to speak with candidates who can demonstrate:
  • A current QBCC Site Supervisor Licence (Open Class) or QBCC Builder Licence (Open Class)
  • Experience supervising multi-trade construction projects involving concrete, structural steel, electrical and earthworks
  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, construction specifications and relevant Australian Standards
  • Sound knowledge of WHS legislation, risk management and site compliance
  • Strong communication, leadership and problem-solving skills
  • Commercial awareness across labour utilisation, subcontractor performance, costs and project variations
  • A current White Card and driver licence
  • Willingness to travel and work a 3 weeks on / 1 week off FIFO or DIDO roster
Experience delivering projects in regional, remote or agricultural environments will be highly regarded.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to join an innovative Australian business and take ownership of varied construction projects across regional and rural Australia. Earthscape is at an exciting stage of its growth, and this is an ideal time to join the team in this key leadership role.  Run projects in the crowded city or out in beautiful regional Australia....that's an easy decision.

Please apply via the “Apply for this job” button or online at www.beilbydt.com.au. For further information, please contact Mark Turner on 0401 404 451.

job.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Research & Learning Lead-Juukan Gorge Legacy Foundation
job.description:
The Foundation

The Juukan Gorge Legacy Foundation was established in May 2023. The Foundation’s purpose is to support the Puutu Kunti Kurrama People (and Pinikura People and other Aboriginal People), by:
  • Building the Puutu Kunti Kurrama community to be strong and proud internally and externally;
  • Providing programs and services that promote and protect traditional law and custom, language and culture, and maintaining and strengthening traditional connection to Country;
  • Providing programs and services that support community health, well-being, and self-determination; and
  • Fostering economic development of projects and industries for financial independence.
The Role

Reporting to the Director Programs & Impact, the Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) Lead will be responsible for developing and embedding the Foundation's approach to understanding, demonstrating and improving its impact. Your role will be to use evidence and learning to strengthen program design, guide investment decisions and adapt organisational practice.

The Person

If you are committed to supporting the aspirations of Traditional Owners, and bring experience in designing and implementing practical MERL frameworks, we would be interested in hearing from you. The ability to translate complex information into practical insights and meaningful outcomes is essential, as is excellent analytical abilities and written and verbal communication skills.

The Package

This is an opportunity to make a significant contribution to the lives of current and future Foundation beneficiaries and First Nations People. In return, a permanent contract is on offer and a base salary of $120,000 to $130,000 plus superannuation. Salary packaging is available and flexible working arrangements are by negotiation. This role is to be based either in the West Perth office or the Pilbara, to be negotiated for the successful candidate.

Applications

job.title: Commercial Lead
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a well-funded Australian resources company advancing a large-scale gold development project in Western Australia. With a high-quality asset, significant growth plans and a strong leadership team, the business is entering an exciting phase as it progresses from project development toward construction and future operations.
Recognised for its entrepreneurial culture and commitment to excellence, the organisation offers the rare opportunity to join a project at a defining stage and contribute directly to its long-term success.

The Opportunity

As the organisation continues its transition from project development toward construction and future operations, an exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Commercial Lead to join a high-performing project team.
Reporting to the Commercial Manager, this role will play a critical part in shaping the commercial foundations of a major Western Australian resources project. Working across procurement, contracting, commercial governance and risk management, you will support the delivery of key project work packages and help drive commercial outcomes that support successful project execution.
This is a hands-on position within a lean owner's team environment, offering broad accountability, direct exposure to senior leadership and the opportunity to influence key decisions throughout a pivotal stage of the project's evolution. You will work closely with technical, project and operational stakeholders, leading tender processes, negotiating high-value contracts and ensuring commercial strategies are aligned with the broader development objectives of the business.

Key Responsibilities
  • Help develop and execute procurement and contracting strategies for major project work packages
  • Lead tendering, contract negotiations and ongoing contract administration activities
  • Provide commercial guidance across project delivery, cost control, governance and risk management processes
  • Manage contractor and supplier relationships while driving value, performance and commercial outcomes
  • Support project teams in evaluating commercial opportunities, claims and contractual risks
About You

You are a commercially astute professional with demonstrated experience supporting large-scale mining, resources, infrastructure or energy projects. You bring strong expertise in contract development, procurement, negotiations and commercial risk management, together with the ability to build productive relationships across multidisciplinary teams. You are comfortable operating in a dynamic project environment, can balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution, and enjoy taking ownership of outcomes.
Experience working within owner's teams, project development environments or major capital projects will be highly regarded. Tertiary qualifications in law, commerce, engineering, quantity surveying or a related discipline are preferred.

Why This Role?

This is a rare opportunity to join a project at a defining stage of its development and contribute to decisions that will shape its future success. You will work alongside an experienced leadership team, gain exposure to major commercial and contracting activities, and have the opportunity to influence how a significant resource development is delivered. The role offers strong professional growth, meaningful responsibility and the chance to be part of a high-performing team focused on creating long-term value.

To Apply

Please apply via the “Apply for this job” button or online at www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference number 1254238.  For initial enquiries or assistance with your application, please contact Nick Verkerk at nverkerk@beilbydt.com.au or Victoria Vieilledent at vvieilledent@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Recruitment - Government Recruitment and Selection
job.description:
About the Opportunity

Beilby Downing Teal has partnered with the WA public sector in delivering trusted recruitment and HR solutions for over 25 years. Due to unprecedented growth, we are now seeking experienced Recruitment Consultants to join our Perth Government Practice to work with government agencies in selecting suitably skilled staff through an objective and robust section process.

This is an opportunity to play a trusted, independent role, working with selection panels  in ensuring candidate evidence, panel deliberations and appointment recommendations are documented accurately, objectively and professionally.

You will work across varied assignments, from shortlisting and interviews through to referee checks and final selection reports ensuring selection panels reach defensible, merit-based decisions in accordance with the Public Sector Management Act and Commissioners Instructions.
The main function of your role will be to:
  • Facilitate panel briefings, shortlisting meetings, interviews and final deliberations.
  • Capture accurate, objective notes of candidate evidence and panel discussions.
  • Guide panels in applying approved selection criteria consistently and in accordance with internal policies.
  • Prepare shortlisting matrices, interview summaries, referee-check records and selection reports.
  • Document comparative assessments, conclusions and recommendations clearly.
  • Incorporate feedback and finalise high-quality documents within agreed deadlines.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality, impartiality and secure information handling.
About you

We are seeking experienced recruitment consultants with a good understanding of the WA Public Sector Management Act and merit-based recruitment.

We would love to hear from you if you have:
  • Experience supporting government or public sector recruitment and selection processes.
  • Excellent writing, note-taking, analytical and report-preparation skills.
  • A sound understanding of merit, equity, procedural fairness and confidentiality.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to work independently and accurately under pressure.
  • Professional judgement and confidence working with senior panel members.
  • Responsiveness, discretion and the ability to meet tight deadlines.
Highly regarded
  • Knowledge of relevant government employment frameworks and recruitment policies.
  • Experience in job classification / design.
  • Experience with executive, specialist, bulk or high-volume recruitment.
Why work with us?

These roles offer flexible, assignment-based hours rather than a fixed weekly schedule. You can choose assignments and working hours that suit your availability, provided you can meet the agreed client requirements and deadlines.
Working primarily from your home office, you will enjoy autonomy, exposure to a broad range of government recruitment processes and the opportunity to contribute to fair and transparent public sector appointments.
Each engagement includes a clear brief, agreed templates and defined deliverables, with support from an experienced administration team and supportive colleagues.

Apply now

If you are an experienced public sector recruitment professional with exceptional writing skills and a commitment to impartiality, we would welcome your application. 
Please apply online at www.beilbydt.com.au by submitting a cover letter and resume (Word or PDF format) and quoting reference number 1257038.
For further information, please contact Denise Wetherall, National General Manager – Government on 0408 000 109 or dwetherall@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Senior Field Service Engineer
job.description:
The Company

Innovation has been at the heart of our clients business since 1889 — from pioneering magnetic separation to redefining non‑ferrous metal recovery and sensor‑based sorting. Today, they combine proven technologies with data‑driven insights, empower customers to unlock new value, recover high‑quality secondary raw materials, and build highly profitable circular economies.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the National Sales Manager, the Senior Field Service Engineer will be responsible for delivering comprehensive after‑sales technical support to customers throughout the full lifecycle of their equipment. This includes installation and commissioning, planned maintenance, unplanned breakdown support, and the programming and optimisation of sorting systems.
After‑sales support may be provided either on site or remotely, including phone-based assistance and remote maintenance access to customer equipment, depending on the situation.

About you

We are seeking an experienced Senior Technician who enjoys commissioning new equipment, providing on‑site servicing, delivering technical support, and building strong customer relationships.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate experience in the following areas:
  • Strong electrical expertise, particularly in electrical control systems. A technical degree or diploma in an electrical discipline is highly regarded.
  • Proven fault‑finding and diagnostic skills, with hands‑on experience responding to and resolving breakdown situations.
  • Solid mechanical knowledge, with the ability to work confidently across electrical and mechanical systems.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly, sometimes at short notice, including international travel to Germany, the USA, New Zealand, and South East Asia.
  • Flexibility to work outside standard business hours on occasion, including weekends, as operational requirements demand with overtime rates provided.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical issues to internal teams and customers alike, ensuring expectations are effectively managed.
Why this role

The successful candidate will be provided an excellent compensation package including international training ( Germany ) and career growth. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply via the “Apply for this job” button or through our website at www.beilbydt.com.au, quoting reference number 1256160. For further inquiries, please contact Aaron Hooper at ahooper@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Manager Finance - Shire of Irwin
job.description:
THE SHIRE

The Shire of Irwin is located on the stunning Batavia Coast, where the historic twin towns of Dongara and Port Denison offer an enviable lifestyle, a welcoming community and a diverse local economy positioned for sustainable growth. Home to approximately 3,800 residents and spanning 2,223 km² of coastal and rural landscapes, this is an opportunity to join a progressive local government at an important time of organisational development and community investment.

THE OPPORTUNITY

A rewarding leadership opportunity is available for an experienced finance professional who can combine strong technical capability with practical, forward-looking strategic advice. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and participating as a key member of the executive leadership team, the Manager Finance will help shape the organisation’s direction. The role will assess proposals, model options, challenge assumptions and advise Council, the CEO and managers on long-term financial sustainability, service delivery, major projects and investment priorities.

THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE

We are seeking a confident and capable leader from a commercial, operational or local government background with:
  • A demonstrated record of providing strategic financial advice to senior leaders and governing bodies;
  • Strong experience in long-term financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and scenario modelling;
  • The ability to translate complex financial information into clear options and practical recommendations;
  • A collaborative approach to business partnering and strengthening organisation-wide financial accountability;
  • Proven experience leading and developing a capable, service-oriented finance team;
  • Tertiary qualifications in Accounting, Finance, Commerce or a related discipline, with strong knowledge of Australian Accounting Standards and the ability to rapidly acquire and apply Western Australian local government financial requirements.
The position leads budgeting, long-term financial planning, statutory reporting, rates, treasury, taxation, financial systems and internal financial controls. Day-to-day payroll administration is managed outside the Finance Department, allowing the role to focus on strategic leadership, organisational support and continuous improvement. Eligibility for CPA Australia or CA ANZ membership will be highly regarded.

THE PACKAGE

In return you will receive a three-to-five-year contract, a competitive base salary, negotiable depending on experience, plus company vehicle, additional superannuation and benefits. The successful candidate will have the option of living full time in Shire accommodation or adopting a hybrid working arrangement, providing the flexibility of working remotely for most of the time, with visiting the Shire regularly to stay connected with the team in person. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone to progress their career and join the Shire at this pivotal time.

To apply please click the Apply Now button or visit www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference 1248622 and provide a comprehensive resume and a covering letter of no more than two pages, specifically addressing each of the six selection criteria in Section 7.0 within the Application Pack, using concise examples of relevant experience and achievements.
